course.title: Data Analytics — Complete Deep Course
course.description: A Data Analytics-specific, beginner-to-advanced course with detailed concepts, practical analysis, dedicated tasks, validation, interpretation and a complete learning-platform capstone.
course.curriculumPolicy: Module and lesson counts are determined by the concepts required to learn the discipline properly; no fixed cross-domain template is imposed.
learningOutcomes: Clean, query, analyze or model data appropriately.

modules.title: Analytics Foundations
modules.description: Business questions, metrics, dimensions, measures, KPIs and the difference between descriptive and diagnostic analysis.

lessons.title: Analytics Foundations
lessons.description: Business questions, metrics, dimensions, measures, KPIs and the difference between descriptive and diagnostic analysis.
learningObjectives: Apply the technique to realistic learning data.

notes.text: Business questions, metrics, dimensions, measures, KPIs and the difference between descriptive and diagnostic analysis.

Learn analytics foundations by connecting the concept to a real data question. First understand what the data represents, then perform the operation, validate the result, and finally explain what the result means.

Analytics Foundations is useful when turning raw learning-platform data into reliable information, decisions or predictive models. The student should understand both the technical operation and the meaning of the result.

notes.caption: Add a teaching diagram showing the data flow for Analytics Foundations.

items: Understand the shape and meaning of the data.
Interpret the result without overstating it.

notes.code:
Scenario: Turn learning-platform business questions into measurable analytics questions.

Example workflow: define the question -> inspect data -> transform/analyze -> validate -> interpret -> document limitations.

items: Check sample sizes and missing values.
State limitations before making a decision.
Using a metric without defining it.
Building a model before defining the business problem.
Reporting a number without explaining uncertainty or limitations.
I can explain Analytics Foundations in my own words.
I can apply it to a small dataset.
I can identify at least one limitation.
I can explain what decision the result can and cannot support.
